messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: exon array cdfs
parts:
Hello all,

I just wanted to let people know that I have made cdfs corresponding
to the Affy annotation from Sept. 14, 2007 (corresponding to the
annotation with the NetAffx Affy software). The links are available on
under the 'Documentation on cdf types' in the pages for the exon
array. These cdfs have not been extensively tested; they do not,
however, have the replicate probe assignments that exist in the
previous cdfs (see documentation pages if this makes no sense to you).
And like the previous cdfs, the large control probesets are not
included.

Note: Affy released new annotation in November right after I finished
these cdfs(!) so these cdfs do not corresond to the latest annotation;
I am in the process of making the corresponding cdfs.

There is a cdf corresponding to core, extended and full probesets, as
well as two new cdfs: a cdf for main design probesets (so also free
and ambiguous probesets) and a cdf with only Affy designated control
probesets (but not necessarily the long ones from the full Affy that
have created problems) I have yet to explore what is here, but they
consist of things like genomic background probes, intron/exon probes
for housekeeping genes; etc. They should not correspond to grid
aligning probes, for example, but again I haven't check them.

Also, please contact me if you discover a problem in the cdf. These
should be considered 'beta' as I have not done extensive checking. I
don't know when I will be able to do this, so I decided to make it
available now.

Best,
Elizabeth

P.S. I have a program for taking a file with probeset annotation as to
what probeset goes with what gene/transcript cluster and converting
the default Affy cdf (with only exon probesets and no gene
definitions) into a gene and exon cdf. This does not reassign probes
to different probesets, so the exon definitions of Affy stay intact
for better or worse. If this of interest to you, please contact me via
the google group. If you want to start at the probe level and make
your own exon definitions, it is possible that someone has a program
for that too.
